steps.title: The Character studio
steps.body: The Characters workspace dresses minifigures (hair, face, outfit, colors, gear) and animates them with keyframe clips. The hero and every neighbour are characters.

steps.title: A new character
steps.body: Start from one of v68's presets: + New character shows a picture of each one; click the one you want. The copy is yours to change; presets themselves stay as they are.
steps.task: Click + New character, then click a preset’s picture.

steps.title: Change the look
steps.body: The properties on the right change every part of the look; the preview updates at once. Each choice (hair, hat, shirt…) is a button with a picture: it opens a panel of pictures of your character wearing each option. Colors are color boxes. Each change is one undo step.
steps.task: Rename the character Robin, then give it a cowboy hat.

how.text: In the panel “Character” (right), click the box “Name”, select its text, type Robin and press Enter. The title above the preview and the name in the list on the left change to Robin.

do.say: Type Robin in the box “Name” (right) and press Enter.

how.text: Scroll the same panel to the section “Face & hair” and click the button “Hat” (it shows a small picture of the hat your character wears now). A panel of pictures opens: your character wearing each hat.

do.say: Click the button “Hat” under “Face & hair”: a panel of hat pictures opens.

how.text: In that panel, click the picture “Cowboy hat”. The panel closes, the preview wears the cowboy hat, and the button “Hat” now reads “Cowboy hat”.

do.say: Click the picture “Cowboy hat”: the preview wears it.

steps.title: The player character
steps.body: One character is the hero the player controls. “Make player character” (or Project tab › Hero) picks it.
steps.task: Make your character the player character.

steps.title: Animation clips
steps.body: Clips are keyframe animations on a timeline: a lane per joint (track), keys (◆) that say where the joint is at a moment, and markers that send events, play sounds or start cinematics. Between two keys the joint moves smoothly. Keys 1–4 play the hero’s emotes in Play.
steps.task: Make a new clip: Clips › + New (left).

doItForMe.say: Click + New next to Clips (left). The new clip opens with an empty timeline under the preview.

how: In the panel on the left, scroll down to Clips and click + New (right of the word Clips). A clip called New clip is made and opens: the timeline appears under the preview.

steps.title: Animate the clip
steps.body: Animating means adding keys: at a moment of the clip, set where a joint is. Here the right arm goes up at 1 second and back down at the end, so the clip lifts the arm and drops it again, over and over (Loop).
steps.task: Make the right arm rise and fall: add the track “Right arm · z”, then a key at 1 second with the value 2.6, then press “Play”.

how.text: Your new clip must be open: it is highlighted under “Clips › Mine” (left), and its timeline is under the preview, starting at 0.00 / 2.00 s. If it is not, click it there.

do.say: Your clip is open: highlighted under Clips › Mine, with its timeline under the preview.

how.text: In the timeline tools (the bar just under the preview), open the drop-down “+ Track…” and pick “Right arm · z”. A lane named “Right arm · z” appears with a key ◆ at 0 s (value 0); it is selected, so the preview rings the right arm and names it.

do.say: Open “+ Track…” in the timeline tools and pick “Right arm · z”: a lane appears with a key at 0 s.

how.text: Click the lanes area halfway across, so the time at the left of the timeline tools reads about 1.00 / 2.00 s. The thin playhead line moves there and the clip stops playing.

do.say: Click halfway across the lanes: the playhead moves to 1.00 s.

how.text: Click the button “◆ Key” in the timeline tools. A second key ◆ appears on the “Right arm · z” lane, at the playhead (1 s).

do.click: [aria-label="Timeline tools"] button[title="Key the selected track at the playhead"]
do.say: Click “◆ Key”: a key appears at 1 s on the Right arm · z lane.

how.text: Click that new key ◆ (at 1 s) to select it. Under the lanes, click the box “value”, select its text, type 2.6 and press Enter. The number 2.6 now shows next to the key on the lane, and the arm is up at 1 s.

do.say: Click the key at 1 s to select it.
In the box “value” under the lanes, type 2.6 and press Enter: the arm goes up at 1 s.

how.text: Press the button “Play” at the top right of the preview. The arm rises and falls as the clip loops. Add more tracks the same way (for example “Right elbow · bend” or “Head · turn”).

do.say: Press “Play” at the top right of the preview: the arm rises and falls.
